correctness.rationale: Let q_i=ρ_i^-2 and c_i²=1-q_i. If some q_i+q_j>1 then c_i²+c_j²<1, so there is an open positive quadrant unit-circle arc u=(a,b) with a>c_i,b>c_j. Choose a nearby distinct nonparallel u′ also on the arc, with w=(u′-u)/2 small enough that z=√(1-||w||²)>c_k. The unit vectors v1=(u,0),v2=(-u′,0),v3=(w,z),v4=(w,-z) sum to zero and any first three span R³; they positively span R³ and satisfy all six strict vertex tests. The inspected Ivanov–Strachan cap-body lemma extends vertex+positive-spanning illumination to the entire body. Every 3D body needs at least four directions. If all pair inequalities are equalities then q_i=1/2 all i; each unit direction can strictly illuminate at most one of the six spikes, so at least six, achieved by coordinate directions.
